    //==
    // # Bounds and vertex centroid of a point-set shape
    //
    // The two obligations a `IPointSet2D` / `IPointSet3D` implementor gets for free from
    // its defining point list, folded through the reductions above. No
    // per-element conveniences are defined here:
    // the defining points are an Array (IIndexable), so `self.Points.IsEmpty`,
    // `self.Points.First`, `self.Points.Count` and `self.Points.At(i)` already come from
    // P2's generics, and re-spelling them at this layer would be pure rule-11
    // duplication.

    //==
    // # PointSet bounds
    //
    // The one measure that is genuinely shared by every point-set shape: the
    // axis-aligned bounds of a shape whose defining points are its extreme points.
    // That holds for every implementor in this tree — segments, triangles, quads,
    // polylines and polygons are all contained in the convex hull of their listed
    // points, and each listed point lies on the shape, so the bounds are TIGHT.
    // (Quad3D's bilinear patch is likewise contained in the hull of its corners.)
    // Shapes whose extent is NOT determined by a stored point list — circles,
    // capsules, cylinders, tori — supply their own body in their declaration file.

    // The tightest axis-aligned rectangle containing the shape.
    Bounds(self: IPointSet2D): Bounds2D
        => self.Points.BoundsOfPoints;

    // The tightest axis-aligned box containing the shape.
    Bounds(self: IPointSet3D): Bounds3D
        => self.Points.BoundsOfPoints;

    //==
    // # PointSet vertex centroid
    //
    // The arithmetic mean of a shape's defining points, folded over the Points
    // array. This is the centroid of the VERTICES as equal point masses, NOT the
    // area/volume-weighted center of mass a ICentroid2D/3D implementor reports; the
    // two differ whenever the vertices are unevenly distributed. Offered on the
    // PointSet surface because it is well defined for any point set, including a
    // scatter with no interior. Precondition: at least one defining point.

    // The vertex centroid of the shape: the arithmetic mean of its defining points.
    VertexCentroid(self: IPointSet2D): Point2D
        => self.Points.AverageOfPoints;

    // The vertex centroid of the shape in space: the arithmetic mean of its points.
    VertexCentroid(self: IPointSet3D): Point3D
        => self.Points.AverageOfPoints;

    //==
    // # IPrimitiveGeometry
    //
    // The primitive-level sibling of the point surface above: whole faces rather
    // than the points inside them. Dispatches on the layer-1 view in
    // `meshes.concepts.plato`, so it serves soups and indexed meshes alike.

    // The number of whole primitives the geometry stores.
    PrimitiveCount(self: IPrimitiveGeometry<$TPoint, $TPrimitive>): Integer
        => self.Primitives.Count;

    //==
    // # Containment, nearest point, and support mapping
    //
    // Bodies for the IContainsPoint2D / 3D, INearestPoint2D / 3D and ISupport2D /
    // 3D interfaces declared in `geometry.concepts.plato`. Distances are computed
    // as the magnitude of a Between delta, so the argument order of Between never
    // affects a distance result.

    //==
    // # IContainsPoint2D / IContainsPoint3D
    //
    // Membership conveniences built on Contains(point). A batched ContainsAll over
    // an Array<Point> is the fold interface-gap noted at the top of the file.

    // True when the point is NOT a member of the shape.
    Excludes(self: IContainsPoint2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => self.Contains(point).Not;

    // True when the point is NOT a member of the shape.
    Excludes(self: IContainsPoint3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => self.Contains(point).Not;

    //==
    // # INearestPoint2D / INearestPoint3D
    //
    // Distance queries built on the nearest-point projection ClosestPoint(point).

    // The straight-line distance from a query point to the nearest point of the shape.
    DistanceTo(self: INearestPoint2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => self.ClosestPoint(point).Between(point).Magnitude;

    // The squared distance to the shape; avoids the square root when only relative
    // distances are compared.
    DistanceToSquared(self: INearestPoint2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => self.ClosestPoint(point).Between(point).MagnitudeSquared;

    // True when the shape lies within `radius` of the query point (inclusive).
    // Compares squared distances, so no square root is taken.
    WithinDistance(self: INearestPoint2D, point: Point2D, radius: Number): Boolean
        => self.DistanceToSquared(point) <= radius * radius;

    // The straight-line distance from a query point to the nearest point of the shape.
    DistanceTo(self: INearestPoint3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.ClosestPoint(point).Between(point).Magnitude;

    // The squared distance to the shape; avoids the square root when only relative
    // distances are compared.
    DistanceToSquared(self: INearestPoint3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.ClosestPoint(point).Between(point).MagnitudeSquared;

    // True when the shape lies within `radius` of the query point (inclusive).
    WithinDistance(self: INearestPoint3D, point: Point3D, radius: Number): Boolean
        => self.DistanceToSquared(point) <= radius * radius;

    //==
    // # ISupport2D / ISupport3D
    //
    // The support mapping returns the farthest point of a convex shape in a given
    // direction (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Support_function). SupportExtent
    // projects that point onto the direction, giving the signed extent of the
    // shape along it — the scalar GJK / SAT actually consume.
    // A `var` local fetches the support point once (LIBRARIES.md permits var locals
    // in statement bodies) instead of re-evaluating Support per component.

    // The signed extent of the shape along `direction`: the support point projected
    // onto the (unit) direction vector.
    SupportExtent(self: ISupport2D, direction: Direction2D): Number
    {
        var p = self.Support(direction);
        return p.X * direction.Vector.X + p.Y * direction.Vector.Y;
    }

    // The signed extent of the shape along `direction`: the support point projected
    // onto the (unit) direction vector.
    SupportExtent(self: ISupport3D, direction: Direction3D): Number
    {
        var p = self.Support(direction);
        return p.X * direction.Vector.X + p.Y * direction.Vector.Y + p.Z * direction.Vector.Z;
    }
}
